The model qualitatively captures the growth rate behaviour observed in simulations and, upon extrapolation to the large ${\rm Pm}$ limit, indicates that $γ$ is only weakly dependent on the resistivity in a PNS. Under conditions relevant to the PNS, this model predicts a magnetic energy growth rate of the order of $\sim 1$ ms$^{-1}$.

entries.title: X-ray to Mid-IR Spectral Energy Distributions: A Catalog of X-ray Selected AGNs in the XMM-COSMOS Survey
entries.abstract: We present a component-resolved analysis of the IR--X-ray connection in a sample of 104 spectroscopically confirmed Type~1 AGN. By combining \xmm, \swift/UVOT, and new high--angular resolution \jwst/NIRCam imaging for a subset of the sources, we constructed detailed SEDs in which the IR emission was explicitly decomposed into accretion-disk, torus, and polar-dust components. This approach enables us to isolate the intrinsic AGN-IR luminosities with minimal host-galaxy contamination, providing a clean assessment of the physical relationship between the accretion flow, circumnuclear dust, and the X-ray corona. By incorporating JWST/NIRCam observations into our SED decomposition, we significantly reduce host-galaxy contamination and isolate the nuclear infrared emission with greater fidelity, particularly at near-infrared (NIR) wavelengths. This improvement is most apparent at 1 $μ\mathrm{m}$, where sources with JWST coverage exhibit a markedly steeper relation between $ν$L$_ν$ (2 keV) and the NIR luminosity than those without JWST data. This behavior is naturally explained by starlight dilution, whereby host-galaxy emission dominates lower-resolution measurements.

entries.title: Spontaneous wandering of the magnetic axis in pulsars: 3D magneto-thermal simulations and the imprint on braking indices
entries.abstract: Braking index measurements of hundreds of pulsars, despite observational caveats, show a clear trend: $n<3$ at early ages, $n>3$ at middle ages, and increasingly large, fluctuating values at larger characteristic ages. Crustal magnetic fields in isolated neutron stars evolve through Ohmic dissipation and non-linear Hall redistribution across scales, with additional early-time contributions from the chiral magnetic effect and post-burial re-emergence. Initial conditions are usually assumed dipole-dominated, whereas more complex and realistic fields, with energy spread more evenly over a broad range of scales, have not been explored in this context. We assess how the internal dynamics of initially non-trivial fields change the dipolar field strength and obliquity, and how their combined contribution to the braking index $n$, together with that of the alignment, compares with the observed values. To this end we perform long-term 3D magneto-thermal simulations, for configurations ranging from the dipole-dominated case to tangled, small-scale-dominated fields. Small-scale dominated configurations with weak dipolar components show rich dynamics: the dipolar mode is continuously fed by the small scales and may grow or decay depending on the initial spectrum, driving $n<3$ or $n>3$, while the obliquity varies on timescales as short as ${\cal O}$(kyr). These spontaneous changes often dominate the alignment torque and can account for the large values of $n-3$ of either sign observed at characteristic ages $τ_c\gtrsim10^5$ yr, unlike the dipole-dominated models. However, short-term magnetospheric fluctuations or superfluid-driven variations of the torque may still be needed to explain the measurements and the structured timing residuals quantitatively. Future work comparing these models with the observed timing properties could fine-tune the most promising initial configurations.

entries.title: Constraints on the central engine of merger-driven long gamma-ray bursts
entries.abstract: Recent observations have identified a new class of long-duration gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) likely produced by compact binary mergers. Using radio observations and lightcurve modelling, we investigate whether a magnetar remnant can power the long-lasting prompt emission observed in this merger-driven GRB sample. We derive constraints on the magnetars' rotational energy and magnetic-field strength, and assess whether the magnetar central-engine model is viable for the observed events. We conducted 2.1 GHz radio observations of seven nearby merger-driven GRBs ($z<0.25$) using the Australia Telescope Compact Array (ATCA), obtaining sensitive upper limits on late-time radio emission 520-6900 days post-burst. We modelled the expected radio light curves from magnetar-energized ejecta interacting with the circumburst medium and compared them to our observations. We separately tested the magnetar hypothesis against the extended gamma-ray emission using a fallback-accreting magnetar model. No radio counterpart is detected in any of the observed GRBs, with 3$σ$ flux density upper limits of 33-72 $μ$Jy at 2.1 GHz. Modelling the expected synchrotron emission from magnetar-energized ejecta interacting with the circumburst medium, we find that the radio non-detections remain compatible with energetic outflows in low-density environments. The analysis of the prompt gamma-ray emission provides complementary constraints on the spin period and magnetic field of the magnetar engine. Once fallback accretion and jet baryon-loading are considered, the parameter space is narrowly confined.

historical_knowledge_points.title: 驻立激波怎样变成一个能量预算约束？
historical_knowledge_points.why_it_matters: 这篇论文的核心判断不是直接拟合某一次耀斑，而是先问震波后的流体是否拥有足够的能量储备。把能量密度、体积、观测辐射能和转换效率分开，有助于读者看清“能量上允许”与“完整辐射机制成立”之间的差别。
historical_knowledge_points.physical_picture: 上游超声速流经过驻立激波后减速、压缩并加热，下游形成更厚、更热的区域。论文用这个下游区域的局部动能损失估计一个可用能量库，再与观测耀斑所需辐射能比较。
assumptions: 流体采用定常、轴对称的低角动量磁化吸积模型。
这里的推导只整理论文的数量级能量估计；没有把热能、磁能和粒子辐射微观过程补进能量库。
声波穿越时间只是把定常模型与耀斑持续时间相连的工作性映射，不是精确的观测时标。

symbols.meaning: 震波前后局部可用动能密度差的数量级估计。
论文定义的压缩比，约为 $\rho_+H_+/(\rho_-H_-)$。
下游流体中可用震波能量储备的估计。
用观测 X 射线光度、持续时间和 bolometric correction 估计的辐射能。
所需震波能量到辐射能的转换分数 $E_{\rm data}/E_{\rm sh}$。

derivation.text: 论文在 Results > Energy budget estimate 中从局部 ram-pressure 能量差开始：$$\delta e_{\rm sh}\propto\rho_-v_-^2-\rho_+v_+^2.$$
论文使用压缩比 $R$、质量流连续条件 $[\rho u^r]=0$ 和厚度比 $\Delta H=H_+/H_-$，将上式写成：$$\delta e_{\rm sh}\propto\rho_-v_-^2\left(1-\frac{\Delta H}{R}\frac{\gamma_{v_-}^2}{\gamma_{v_+}^2}\right).$$

论文在 Results > Energy budget estimate 的 Eq. (fluence) 中将局部能量密度估计乘以准球形震波后区体积，并写出能量储备原式：$$E_{\rm sh}\equiv4\pi\rho_-v_-^2\left(1-\frac{\Delta H}{R}\frac{\gamma_{v_-}^2}{\gamma_{v_+}^2}\right)r_{\rm sh}^2H_+\times M_{\rm BH}c^2.$$
教学补充：把 $r_{\rm sh}^2H_+$ 看作特征体积尺度，再乘以能量密度和单位换算，可以先做量纲检查；这是对论文原式的解释性拆解，不是作者额外给出的独立推导。
论文把观测辐射能写成 $E_{\rm data}=f_{\rm bol}L_{\rm X}\tau_{\rm obs}$，然后定义所需转换分数：$$\epsilon=\frac{E_{\rm data}}{E_{\rm sh}}.$$
教学补充：$\epsilon<1$ 只说明在该估计器下能量储备足以容纳观测辐射能；它不等于模型已经解释了光变、光谱或辐射效率的时间演化。

units_checks: $E_{\rm sh}$ 和 $E_{\rm data}$ 都是能量，因而 $\epsilon$ 无量纲。
$r_{\rm sh}^2H_+$ 给出长度三次方；与能量密度和单位换算相乘后才得到能量。
当 $E_{\rm data}$ 增大而 $E_{\rm sh}$ 固定时，$\epsilon$ 线性增大；这与论文说明 bolometric correction 的不确定性会线性传播一致。
historical_knowledge_points.paper_use: 论文用这个估计器将不同震波分支与 Chandra 耀斑目录的持续时间和能量需求相比较。正文结论是弱耀斑通常只需约 $10^{-3}$--$10^{-2}$ 的效率，中等耀斑需几个百分点；最强事件可能需要额外磁耗散。
